rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clear proof alludes to the knowledge and prophethood God granted Shuʿayb.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما آتاه الله من العلم والنبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good provision alludes to lawful wealth given by God, through His help rather than Shuʿayb's own toil.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى ما آتاه الله من المال الحلال

words: إِن كُنتُ عَلَىٰ بَيِّنَةٍۢ مِّن رَّبِّى وَرَزَقَنِى مِنْهُ رِزْقًا حَسَنًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The omitted conditional answer asks whether he could betray revelation and oppose God's command after such spiritual and bodily favors; it answers objections to changing customs and forbidding ancestral religion.
rows.anchor: وجواب الشرط محذوف تقديره فهل يسع مع هذا الإنعام الجامع للسعادات الروحانية والجسمانية

words: وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنْ أُخَالِفَكُمْ إِلَىٰ مَآ أَنْهَىٰكُمْ عَنْهُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He does not intend to do what he forbids in order to reserve it for himself; if it were right, he would choose it. The idiom distinguishes going toward what another leaves from going away from it.
rows.anchor: لأستبد به دونكم، فلو كان صوابا

words: إِنْ أُرِيدُ إِلَّا ٱلْإِصْلَٰحَ مَا اسْتَطَعْتُ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He wants only to reform his people through commanding right and forbidding wrong as far as he can; if their way were sound, he would not forbid it.
rows.anchor: أن أصلحكم بأمري بالمعروف ونهيي عن المنكر ما دمت أستطيع الإصلاح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The three replies are ordered by the three rights a rational person should observe: God's right first, then the self's, then other people's; each requires his commands and prohibitions.
rows.anchor: التنبيه على أن العاقل يجب أن يراعي في كل ما يأتيه ويذره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ما may be a verbal noun functioning as a time adverb, a relative pronoun apposed to الإصلاح meaning the amount he can manage, or part of an elided construction meaning reform of what he can manage.
rows.anchor: و { ما } مصدرية واقعة موقع الظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: His ability to attain what is true and right comes only through God's guidance and aid.
rows.anchor: وما توفيقي لإصابة الحق والصواب إلا بهدايته ومعونته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Exclusive reliance on God expresses pure monotheism: He alone has power, while everything else is inherently helpless; this is the highest knowledge of the Originator.
rows.anchor: فإنه القادر المتمكن من كل شيء وما عداه عاجز في حد ذاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Turning back to God signifies knowledge of the return to Him, and fronting the prepositional phrase gives the expression an exclusive force.
rows.anchor: إشارة إلى معرفة المعاد، وهو أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These words ask God for right judgment and aid in every affair, declare complete turning to Him, end the unbelievers' hopes, show indifference to their hostility, and warn of return to God for judgment.
rows.anchor: طلب التوفيق لإصابة الحق فيما يأتيه ويذره من الله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes this as the true invocation: God alone deserves worship and calling upon Him.
rows.anchor: الدعاء الحق فإنه الذي يحق أن يعبد ويدعى إلى عبادته دون غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative takes it as the answered invocation, supported by what follows about response to prayer.
rows.anchor: أو له الدعوة المجابة فإن من دعاه أجابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On either reading, حق means the opposite of falsehood; the genitive construction reflects association, or means the invocation of the One who is true.
rows.anchor: و { الحق } على الوجهين ما يناقض الباطل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes الحق as God Himself, making every invocation directed to Him an invocation of truth.
rows.anchor: وقيل { الحق } هو الله تعالى وكل دعاء إليه دعوة الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If the passage concerns Arbad and Amir, their destruction unseen by them is God's answer to the Messenger's prayer or proof that he is truthful.
rows.anchor: إن كانت الآية في أربد وعامر أن إهلاكهما من حيث لم يشعرا به محال من الله إجابة لدعوة رسوله

words: وَمَا دُعَآءُ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On a general reading, the passage threatens unbelievers arguing with the Messenger with destruction or an answered prayer against them, and may also expose their error and unsound judgment.
rows.anchor: وإن كانت عامة فالمراد وعيد الكفرة على مجادلة رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can mean idols called upon by polytheists, with the resumptive pronoun omitted, or polytheists calling idols, with the object omitted because context supplies it.
rows.anchor: أي والأصنام الذين يدعوهم المشركون

words: لَا يَسْتَجِيبُونَ لَهُم بِشَىْءٍ إِلَّا كَبَٰسِطِ كَفَّيْهِ إِلَى ٱلْمَآءِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their gods answer no request; the exception compares them to someone stretching both hands toward water and asking it to reach his mouth, since an idol is insensible and powerless.
rows.anchor: إلا استجابة كاستجابة من بسط كفيه

words: كَبَٰسِطِ كَفَّيْهِ إِلَى ٱلْمَآءِ لِيَبْلُغَ فَاهُ
rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative comparison is to someone who hopes to scoop water to drink but merely opens his hands toward it.
rows.anchor: وقيل شبهوا في قلة جدوى دعائهم لها بمن أراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase is also read with second-person تدعون and with باسط carrying tanwīn.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «تدعون» بالتاء وباسط بالتنوين

words: وَمَا دُعَآءُ ٱلْكَٰفِرِينَ إِلَّا فِى ضَلَٰلٍۢ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The invocation of unbelievers comes to nothing: it is loss and falsehood.
rows.anchor: في ضياع وخسار وباطل

words: وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ طَوْعًۭا وَكَرْهًۭا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prostration may be literal: angels and believing humans prostrate willingly in hardship and ease, while unbelievers do so unwillingly under hardship and necessity.
rows.anchor: فإنه يسجد له الملائكة والمؤمنون من الثقلين

words: وَلِلَّهِ يَسْجُدُ مَن فِى ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the prostration means that people submit to God's bringing about what He wills in them, whether they wish it or not, while their shadows submit to His extending and contracting them.
rows.anchor: وأن يراد به انقيادهم لإحداث ما أراده منهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طوعا وكرها may be circumstantial accusatives or express the cause of prostration.
rows.anchor: وانتصاب { طوعا وكرها } بالحال أو العلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The time phrase may modify يسجد or describe the shadows; the two times can imply permanence, and are specified because shadows grow long and numerous then.
rows.anchor: والمراد بهما الدوام أو حال من الظلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: غدو is the plural of غداة, like قنى from قناة; الآصال is the plural of أصيل, the time between afternoon and sunset. Another reading is الإيصال, entering the evening.
rows.anchor: والغدو جمع غداة كقنى جمع قناة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The water may come from clouds, from the direction of the sky, or from the sky itself, since its origins are from there.
rows.anchor: من السحاب أو من جانب السماء أو من السماء نفسها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أودية means rivers, originally the places where abundant water flows; it is extended to mean the water flowing there. The noun is indefinite because rain alternates between regions.
rows.anchor: أنهار جمع واد وهو الموضع الذي يسيل الماء فيه بكثرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The measure may be what God knows to be beneficial and harmless, or the measure each valley allows according to its size.
rows.anchor: بمقدارها الذي علم الله تعالى أنه نافع غير ضار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The flood raises foam, and رابيا means high or rising; the foam is the scum of boiling.
rows.anchor: { فاحتمل السيل زبدا } رفعه والزبد وضر الغليان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metals encompass gold, silver, iron, and copper; treating them as insignificant displays God's greatness.
rows.anchor: يعم الفلزات كالذهب والفضة والحديد والنحاس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metal is heated to make jewelry or useful articles such as vessels and tools for war or farming, illustrating its benefits.
rows.anchor: أي طلب حلى. { أو متع } كالأواني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The metal produces scum like water foam; من may mark origin or partitive meaning. Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Ḥafṣ read يوقدون with ياء, with the people understood as its subject.
rows.anchor: و { من } للابتداء أو للتبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The parable maps truth to useful, lasting water and metal: water serves many needs and remains in the earth or feeds springs and wells, while metal can be fashioned into durable goods; falsehood is useless and quickly vanishes like foam.
rows.anchor: مثل الحق في إفادته وثباته بالماء الذي ينزل من السماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The foam is cast away by the flood or melted metal; جفاء is circumstantial accusative, and جفالا is another reading with the same sense.
rows.anchor: يجفأ به أي يرمي به السبيل والفلز المذاب

words: وَأَمَّا مَا يَنفَعُ ٱلنَّاسَ فَيَمْكُثُ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What benefits people is water and the purified essence of the metal, which remains in the earth for its inhabitants to use.
rows.anchor: { وأما ما ينفع الناس } كالماء وخلاصة الفلز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God gives parables in this way to make difficult or unclear matters intelligible.
rows.anchor: { كذلك يضرب الله الأمثال } لإيضاح المشتبهات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people were seized by a terrifying, deadly blast; it is also said to have been Gabriel's cry.
rows.anchor: يعني صيحة هائلة مهلكة. وقيل صيحة جبريل عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They were struck as they entered the time of sunrise.
rows.anchor: داخلين في وقت شروق الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Humanity was created from a fluid, insentient and motionless substance that cannot retain a position or shape.
rows.anchor: جماد لا حس بها ولا حراك سيالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: خصيم مبين means an eloquent disputant who makes an argument clear, or one who openly confronts his Creator and asks who can revive decayed bones.
rows.anchor: { مبين } للحجة أو خصيم مكافح لخالقه

rows.speaker: أبي بن خلف
rows.claim: A report says Ubayy ibn Khalaf brought the Prophet a decayed bone, challenged whether God could revive it, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: روي أن أبي بن خلف أتى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم بعظم رميم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Livestock means camels, cattle, and sheep; its mention is governed by an understood verb explained by خلقها لكم, or coordinated with الإنسان.
rows.anchor: الإبل والبقر والغنم وانتصابها بمضمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Warmth means what protects people from cold; benefits include offspring, milk, and riding, with منافع broad enough to include their monetary value.
rows.anchor: ما يدفأ به فيقي البرد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Eating from livestock means their meat, fat, and milk. The phrase is fronted to preserve verse endings or because livestock are the customary staple, unlike other edible animals used medicinally or for pleasure.
rows.anchor: أي تأكلون ما يؤكل منها من اللحوم والشحوم والألبان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Earlier peoples likewise associated partners with God, prohibited what He permitted, and rejected His messengers.
rows.anchor: فأشركوا بالله وحرموا حله وردوا رسله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Messengers must clearly deliver the truth; this mediates guidance but does not itself change the state of one God does not guide.
rows.anchor: إلا الإبلاغ الموضح للحق وهو لا يؤثر في هدى من شاء الله هداه

words: وَلَقَدْ بَعَثْنَا فِى كُلِّ أُمَّةٍۢ رَّسُولًا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What God wills occurs through appointed means; sending messengers to every nation is a divine practice that guides seekers and increases the misguidance of those destined for it.
rows.anchor: وما شاء الله وقوعه إنما يجب وقوعه لا مطلقا بل بأسباب قدرها له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Every messenger called people to worship God and shun the false deity or tyrant.
rows.anchor: يأمر بعبادة الله تعالى واجتناب الطاغوت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guided some by enabling them to believe; others remained astray because He did not grant or will guidance, affirming that settled misguidance is by God's act and will.
rows.anchor: ومنهم من حقت عليه الضللة } إذ لم يوفقهم ولم يرد هداهم

words: فَسِيرُوا۟ فِى ٱلْأَرْضِ فَٱنظُرُوا۟ كَيْفَ كَانَ عَٰقِبَةُ ٱلْمُكَذِّبِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The address tells Quraysh to travel and consider the fate of Aad, Thamud, and other deniers as a lesson.
rows.anchor: { فسيروا فى الأرض } يا معشر قريش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Knowledge of what is hidden in the heavens and earth belongs exclusively to God; the unseen is what is neither perceived nor indicated by something perceived.
rows.anchor: يختص به علمه لا يعلمه غيره

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative interpretation identifies the unseen here as the Day of Resurrection, unknown to heaven's and earth's inhabitants.
rows.anchor: وقيل يوم القيامة فإن علمه غائب عن أهل السموات والأرض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Hour's coming is as quick and easy as an eyelid's return from top to bottom, or nearer still, perhaps in the very instant it begins, since God raises creation at once.
rows.anchor: إلا كرجع الطرف من أعلى الحدقة إلى أسفلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle أو can express a choice between descriptions or mean بل, rather.
rows.anchor: { أو } للتخيير أو بمعنى بل

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further reading says that even if the Hour is delayed, it is as near to God as a blink or nearer, emphasizing its imminence.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه أن قيام الساعة وإن تراخى فهو عند الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's power over everything includes raising creatures at once, as He demonstrated by bringing them into existence gradually from their mothers' wombs.
rows.anchor: فيقدر أن يحيي الخلائق دفعة كما قدر أن أحياهم متدرجا

rows.speaker: الكسائي وحمزة
rows.claim: Al-Kisāʾī reads the hamza of أمهات with kasra as a dialect or by assimilation; Ḥamza reads its hamza, mīm, and hāʾ with kasra, adding a hāʾ like أهراق.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الكسائي بكسر الهمزة على أنه لغة أو إتباع لما قبلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Newborns know nothing and begin in a state of ignorance likened to lifeless matter.
rows.anchor: جهالا مستصحبين جهل الجمادية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hearing, sight, and hearts let people sense particulars, recognize likenesses and differences through repeated perception, gain self-evident knowledge, and acquire further knowledge by reasoning.
rows.anchor: أداة تتعلمون بها فتحسون بمشاعركم جزئيات الأشياء فتدركونها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These faculties are given so people recognize God's successive favors and give thanks.
rows.anchor: كي تعرفوا ما أنعم عليكم طورا بعد طور فتشكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When Moses reached the fire, he found a white flame burning in a green tree and was called by name.
rows.anchor: أي النار وجد نارا بيضاء تتقد في شجرة خضراء

rows.speaker: ابن كثير وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Abū ʿAmr read إني with fatḥa, understood as بأني; the remaining readers use kasra, with القول understood or the call treated as speech.
rows.anchor: فتحه ابن كثير وأبو عمرو أي بأني وكسره الباقون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun is repeated for emphasis and confirmation.
rows.anchor: وتكرير الضمير للتوكيد والتحقيق

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is said that Moses wondered who was speaking; after hearing God identify Himself, Satan suggested it might be a devil, but Moses recognized God's speech because he heard it from every direction and through every limb.
rows.anchor: قيل إنه لما نودي قال: من المتكلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The account points to Moses receiving God's speech spiritually, then its representation reaching his body and common sense without limitation to one organ or direction.
rows.anchor: وهو إشارة إلى أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام تلقى من ربه كلامه تلقيا روحانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Removing the sandals may signify humility and decorum, as early Muslims circumambulated barefoot.
rows.anchor: أمره بذلك لأن الحفوة تواضع وأدب ولذلك طاف السلف حافين

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another explanation is that the sandals were unclean because they were made of untanned donkey hide.
rows.anchor: وقيل لنجاسة نعليه فإنهما كانتا من جلد حمار غير مدبوغ

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A figurative interpretation reads the command as emptying the heart of family and possessions.
rows.anchor: وقيل معناه فرغ قلبك من الأهل والمال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The holy valley explains why the place should be treated with reverence; المقدس can bear both senses discussed for holiness.
rows.anchor: تعليل للأمر باحترام البقعة والمقدس يحتمل المعنيين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: طوى is an explanatory apposition for the valley; Ibn ʿĀmir and the Kufans read it with tanwīn, construing it as a place name.
rows.anchor: عطف بيان للوادي ونونه ابن عامر والكوفيون بتأويل المكان

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Alternatively, طوى is like ثنى, a verbal noun from folding, describing two calls or a place sanctified twice.
rows.anchor: وقيل هو كثني من الطي مصدر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God chose Moses for prophethood.
rows.anchor: اصطفيتك للنبوة

rows.speaker: حمزة
rows.claim: Ḥamza reads وإنا اخترناك with plural suffix and a different initial form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة «وإنا اخترناك»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is to listen to what is revealed, meaning either the content revealed to him or the revelation itself.
rows.anchor: للذي يوحى إليك، أو للوحي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām may attach to either of the two preceding verbs.
rows.anchor: واللام تحتمل التعلق بكل من الفعلين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The declaration is apposition to what is revealed and restricts it to affirming monotheism, the highest knowledge, alongside worship, the perfection of action.
rows.anchor: بدل مما يوحى دال على أنه مقصور على تقرير التوحيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prayer is singled out and commanded because its purpose is remembering God, engaging heart and tongue in His remembrance.
rows.anchor: خصها بالذكر وأفردها بالأمر للعلة التي أناط بها إقامتها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: One interpretation takes the phrase to mean that God mentioned prayer in scripture and commanded it.
rows.anchor: وقيل { لذكرى } لأني ذكرتها في الكتب وأمرت بها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another interpretation takes it to mean that God will remember Moses with praise.
rows.anchor: أو لأن أذكرك بالثناء

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: A further interpretation means remembering God alone, without ostentation or mixing His remembrance with another's.
rows.anchor: أو { لذكرى } خاصة لا ترائي بها ولا تشوبها

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Other interpretations take it as praying at times appointed for remembrance or as remembering one's prayer.
rows.anchor: وقيل لأوقات ذكري وهي مواقيت الصلاة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic report says whoever sleeps through or forgets a prayer should perform it when remembering it, citing God's command to establish prayer for His remembrance.
rows.anchor: لما روي أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is to go to Pharaoh with the two signs and call him to worship.
rows.anchor: بهاتين الآيتين وادعه إلى العبادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh had rebelled and acted arrogantly.
rows.anchor: { إنه طغى } عصى وتكبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier commission addressed Moses alone, while this one addresses Moses and Aaron, so the wording is not redundant. Aaron may have been told to meet Moses, or may have heard of his approach and gone to meet him.
rows.anchor: أمر به أولا موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام وحده وههنا إياه وأخاه فلا تكرير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Gentle speech resembles an invitation framed as an offer and counsel; this avoids provoking Pharaoh's violence or may show respect for his having raised Moses.
rows.anchor: فإنه دعوة في صورة عرض ومشورة حذرا أن تحمله الحماقة

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: It is said they addressed Pharaoh by one of his three kunyas: Abu al-Abbas, Abu al-Walid, or Abu Murra.
rows.anchor: وقيل كنياه وكان له ثلاث كنى

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: Another report says they promised him everlasting youth and a kingdom that would last until his death.
rows.anchor: وقيل عداه شبابا لا يهرم بعده وملكا لا يزول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The hope clause may modify ذهبا or قولا, telling them to act in hope their effort will bear fruit; the hopeful exerts himself, unlike the despairing person who only pretends to act.
rows.anchor: متعلق ب { اذهبا } أو «قولا» أي: باشرا الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The mission establishes proof, removes excuses, and displays signs; remembrance is hoped for if truth is recognized, while fear may still arise if it is suspected, hence the order of the verbs.
rows.anchor: الفائدة في إرسالهما والمبالغة عليهما في الاجتهاد مع علمه بأنه لا يؤمن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They fear Pharaoh will hasten to punish them before their mission is completed and the miracle shown; فرط means to go ahead, as in a forerunner or a horse that outruns others.
rows.anchor: أن يعجل علينا بالعقوبة ولا يصبر إلى تمام الدعوة وإظهار المعجزة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reading from أفرطته means someone incites Pharaoh to haste, whether arrogance, fear for his rule, or a human or jinn devil; another reading means excess in harming them.
rows.anchor: وقرىء { يفرط } من أفرطته إذا حملته على العجلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They also fear Pharaoh will grow more tyrannical and, through insolence and harshness, say what is improper of God.
rows.anchor: أو أن يزداد طغيانا فيتخطى إلى أن يقول فيك ما لا ينبغي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's presence with them means His protection and victory.
rows.anchor: { قال لا تخافا إنني معكما } بالحفظ والنصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God hears and sees everything said and done between them and Pharaoh, intervening to repel harm and grant victory; alternatively, the words describe Him as their capable, hearing, seeing protector.
rows.anchor: ما يجري بينكما وبينه من قول وفعل، فأحدث في كل ما يصرف شره عنكما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The demand is that Pharaoh release the Israelites.
rows.anchor: فأرسل معنا بنى إسرءيل } أطلقهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their mistreatment includes onerous labor and killing male children in alternating years while the Israelites were held by the Copts.
rows.anchor: بالتكاليف الصعبة وقتل الولدان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mentioning Israel's rescue immediately after arriving shows that saving believers from unbelievers is more important than calling unbelievers to faith; it may instead indicate gradual invitation.
rows.anchor: وتعقيب الإتيان بذلك دليل على أن تخليص المؤمنين من الكفرة أهم من دعوتهم إلى الإيمان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular sign confirms the claim to be messengers; it names proof of the claim rather than counting the signs, as do other passages that use singular sign or proof despite multiple miracles.
rows.anchor: جملة مقررة لما تضمنه الكلام السابق من دعوى الرسالة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The greeting may be the angels' and keepers of Paradise's greeting to the rightly guided, or it may promise them safety in both abodes.
rows.anchor: وسلام الملائكة وخزنة الجنة على المهتدين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The revealed warning states that punishment awaits those who deny the messengers and turn away.
rows.anchor: أن عذاب المنزلين على المكذبين للرسل

words: أَنَّ ٱلْعَذَابَ عَلَىٰ مَن كَذَّبَ وَتَوَلَّىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording changes to explicit, emphatic warning because threat is most useful and important at the start, and suits what will happen.
rows.anchor: ولعل تغيير النظم والتصريح بالوعيد والتوكيد فيه لأن التهديد في أول الأمر أهم وأنجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses inwardly feared either a natural surprise at what he saw or that the people might doubt and fail to follow him.
rows.anchor: فأضمر فيها خوفا من مفاجأته على ما هو مقتضى الجبلة البشرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's assurance that Moses is uppermost explains the command not to fear and emphasizes victory through independent assertion, certainty particle, repeated pronoun, definite predicate, and superlative wording.
rows.anchor: تعليل للنهي وتقرير لغلبته مؤكدا بالاستئناف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leaving the staff unnamed may belittle it beside the magicians' implements, or magnify it: the small object in Moses' hand has greater effect than their large tools.
rows.anchor: أبهمه ولم يقل عصاك تحقيرا لها أي لا تبال بكثرة حبالهم وعصيهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff swallows their tricks through God's power; تلقف derives from تتلقف with one ت omitted, and its prefix can mark feminine agreement or address when the cause is assigned the action.
rows.anchor: تبتلعه بقدرة الله تعالى، وأصله تتلقف

rows.speaker: ابن عامر برواية ابن ذكوان وحفص
rows.claim: Ibn ʿĀmir through Ibn Dhakwān reads the verb in the nominative as a circumstantial clause or new sentence; Ḥafṣ reads it jussive and light, from لقفت meaning تلقفت.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن عامر برواية ابن ذكوان بالرفع على الحال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What they made means what they contrived and fabricated.
rows.anchor: { إنما صنعوا } أن الذي زوروا وافتعلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading puts كيد in the accusative, taking ما as a particle that makes صنعوا transitive.
rows.anchor: وقرىء بالنصب على أن ما كافة وهو مفعول صنعوا

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: Ḥamza and al-Kisāʾī read سحر: it can mean possessor of magic, call a magician magic for emphasis, or explain the genitive as the magic itself.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «سحر» بمعنى ذي سحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular ساحر is generic, as is الساحر in the following clause; al-ʿAjjāj's phrase سعي دنيا illustrates the indefinite construction.
rows.anchor: وإنما وحد الساحر لأن المراد به الجنس المطلق

rows.speaker: العجاج
rows.claim: Al-ʿAjjāj's line يوم ترى النفوس ما أعدت في سعي دنيا طالما قد مدت is cited as evidence for the indefinite construction around سعي دنيا.
rows.anchor: كقول العجاج: يوم ترى النفوس ما أعدت في سعي دنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حيث أتى means wherever he is or wherever he approaches.
rows.anchor: { حيث أتى } حيث كان وأين أقبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The staff swallowed the tricks, making the magicians realize it was God's sign rather than magic; they fell prostrate to God in repentance and reverence.
rows.anchor: فألقى فتلقفت فتحقق عند السحرة أنه ليس بسحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron may be named first because he was older, to fit the verse's cadence, or because Pharaoh had raised Moses and might otherwise be mistaken for the intended lord.
rows.anchor: قدم هارون لكبر سنه أو لروي الآية

rows.speaker: روي
rows.claim: A report says the magicians saw Paradise and their own dwellings there while prostrating.
rows.anchor: روي أنهم رأوا في سجودهم الجنة ومنازلهم فيها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to Moses, and the lām appears because the verb implies following him.
rows.anchor: أي لموسى واللام لتضمن الفعل معنى الاتباع

rows.speaker: قنبل وحفص
rows.claim: Qunbul and Ḥafṣ read the words as a statement; the other readers make them a question.
rows.anchor: وقرأ قنبل وحفص { آمنتم له } على الخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh accuses Moses of being the magicians' master, greatest in their art, or most knowledgeable in it.
rows.anchor: لعظيمكم في فنكم وأعلمكم به أو لأستاذكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Cutting them crosswise means the right hand and left foot; مِن marks the starting point, and the phrase is an accusative circumstantial description of differently paired limbs.
rows.anchor: اليد اليمنى والرجل اليسرى، ومن ابتدائية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Both verbs are also read with light consonants.
rows.anchor: وقرىء «لأقطعن» «ولأصلبن» بالتخفيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording compares the crucified person's firm attachment to the trunk with something held inside its container; Pharaoh was the first to crucify people.
rows.anchor: شبه تمكن المصلوب بالجذع بتمكن المظروف بالظرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh means himself and Moses, as indicated by his saying آمنتم له; the lām with belief in scripture for someone other than God belittles Moses, though Moses did not inflict punishment.
rows.anchor: يريد نفسه وموسى لقوله { آمنتم له } واللام مع الإيمان في كتاب الله

rows.speaker: قيل
rows.claim: An alternative takes the comparison to be with the Lord of Moses, whom the magicians believed.
rows.anchor: وقيل رب موسى الذي آمنوا به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أبقى means more enduring in punishment.
rows.anchor: { أشد عذابا وأبقى } وأدوم عقابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people say they will remain devoted to the calf until Moses returns; their answer supports the first interpretation.
rows.anchor: على العجل وعبادته. { عكفين } مقيمين. { حتى يرجع إلينا موسى }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses addresses Aaron after returning.
rows.anchor: أي قال له موسى حين رجع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses may ask why Aaron did not join him in anger for God and fight the idolaters, or why he did not follow in his footsteps and catch up.
rows.anchor: أن تتبعني في الغضب لله والمقاتلة مع من كفر به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, ألا تتبعن means follow me or catch up with me; لا may be extra as in the question at 7:12.
rows.anchor: و «لا» مزيدة كما في قوله ما منعك ألا تسجد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses means Aaron failed to stand firm in religion and defend it.
rows.anchor: بالصلابة في الدين والمحاماة عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron invokes their mother rather than their father to soften Moses; it is also said they shared only a mother, while the majority say they shared both parents.
rows.anchor: خص الأم استعطافا وترقيقا، وقيل لأنه كان أخاه من الأم

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority hold that Aaron and Moses were full brothers.
rows.anchor: والجمهور على أنهما كانا من أب وأم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses seized Aaron by his beard and head hair, overcome with fierce anger for God when he saw the calf worship; he was naturally stern and forceful.
rows.anchor: أي بشعر رأسي قبض عليهما يجره إليه من شدة غيظه وفرط غضبه لله

words: إِنِّى خَشِيتُ أَن تَقُولَ فَرَّقْتَ بَيْنَ بَنِىٓ إِسْرَٰٓءِيلَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron feared Moses would accuse him of dividing Israel if he fought the calf worshippers or split the people into factions.
rows.anchor: لو قاتلت أو فارقت بعضهم ببعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aaron did not disregard Moses' instruction to succeed him and set things right; reform meant preserving and accommodating the masses until Moses returned.
rows.anchor: حين قلت { اخلفني في قومي وأصلح } فإن الإصلاح كان في حفظ الدهماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Do not gaze at others' possessions with admiration or wish to possess them.
rows.anchor: { ولا تمدن عينيك } أي نظر عينيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase means categories of unbelievers; it may also describe the pronoun in به, with منهم as the object and the possessions understood as belonging to some groups or people.
rows.anchor: { أزوجا منهم } وأصنافا من الكفرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: زهرة الحياة الدنيا may be governed by an elided verb indicated by متعنا or به, apposed to the object or أزواجا with an implied noun, or used as a rebuke; it means worldly adornment and splendor.
rows.anchor: منصوب بمحذوف دل عليه { متعنا } أو { به } على تضمينه معنى أعطينا

rows.speaker: يعقوب
rows.claim: Yaʿqūb reads the word with fatḥa, either a dialect form or a collective meaning worldly flourish, depicting their finery in contrast with believers' asceticism.
rows.anchor: وقرأ يعقوب بالفتح وهو لغة كالجهرة في الجهرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The worldly gifts may be a trial or a means of punishment in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أو لنعذبهم في الآخرة بسببه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord's provision may be what He has stored for the addressee in the afterlife, or the guidance and prophethood He has granted.
rows.anchor: وما ادخر لك في الآخرة، أو ما رزقك من الهدى والنبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Lord's provision is better than what unbelievers receive in this world and does not end.
rows.anchor: { خير } مما منحهم في الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command is for the Prophet to tell his household or followers to pray, so they can seek help with hardship and avoid preoccupation with livelihood or the habits of the wealthy.
rows.anchor: أمره بأن يأمر أهل بيته أو التابعين له من أمته بالصلاة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Persist in prayer and keep it up.
rows.anchor: { واصطبر عليها } وداوم عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God does not require the Prophet to provide for himself or his family; God provides for them so he can devote his attention to the afterlife.
rows.anchor: { لا نسألك رزقا } أي أن ترزق نفسك ولا أهلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The good outcome belongs to the people of piety.
rows.anchor: المحمودة. { للتقوى } لذوي التقوى

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report says that when the Prophet's family suffered hardship, he would instruct them to pray and recite this verse.
rows.anchor: أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام كان إذا أصاب أهله ضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They may demand a sign proving his prophethood or a sign they propose, rejecting existing signs out of stubbornness and hostility.
rows.anchor: بآية تدل على صدقه في إهداء النبوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur'an answers them as the mother of miracles, greatest and most enduring, because knowledge outranks action in status and lasting effect, and a prophetic miracle is extraordinary knowledge or action.
rows.anchor: فألزمهم بإتيانه بالقرآن الذي هو أم المعجزات وأعظمها وأبقاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier scriptures include the Torah, Gospel, and other revealed books. Their essentials of belief and universal law appear in the Qur'an brought by an unlettered man who had not studied them, a clear miracle; earlier books require proof of authenticity.
rows.anchor: من التوراة والإنجيل وسائر الكتب السماوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الصحف is also read with a light consonant; Nāfiʿ, Abū ʿAmr, and Ḥafṣ read تأتهم with تاء, while the other readers use ياء.
rows.anchor: وقرىء »الصحف« بالتخفيف وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو
